transcript:
Meeting header
Date: 2026-10-30
Start: 15:00 PT | Duration: 57m
Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Jonah (Redwood SE), Priya (Redwood Partners), Ethan (CloudMarket Channel), Lina (CloudMarket SE), Markus (CloudMarket VP Alliances)

Summary:
Quick partner GTM alignment and deal prioritization for North America Q4 co-sell sprint. Cover pilot selection, technical benchmark plan, margin/resale mechanics, security/compliance gating, and next steps for a partner-led pilot.

[00:00] Maya: Hey everyone, thanks for jumping on. Quick round—who's on from CloudMarket?
[00:07] Ethan: Hey, Ethan here — Channel. Lina and Markus are on as well. Good to see you all.
[00:12] Maya: Awesome. We'll run through a short agenda: priorities, pilot candidates, technical runbook, pricing/resale discussion, then next steps. Jonah will jump into benchmarks.
[00:22] Jonah: Hi team, quick note — we'll propose a 48 hour benchmark window that exercises p50/p95 and cost/unit with prefix caching on typical marketplace flows.
[00:31] Markus: Sounds promising. Two constraints from our side: 1) the partner compensation has to be clear up front, and 2) we need a cert'd security doc for enterprise customers — SOC2 and KMS integration notes.
[00:42] Priya: We'll get the SOC2 packet and KMS integration guide. Redwood has a private deployment path too, which we can mention for customers with strict data residency.

[00:55] Ethan: On the co-sell front — our sales teams are worried about margin compression if we resell too low. We need examples of resale pricing that keep us motivated.
[01:04] Maya: Totally. We'll share a partner pricing matrix showing hosted vs dedicated margins and an example SOW for a pilot so you can see how economics flow.
[01:12] Lina: From a technical seat, we care about latency and token cost. Our marketplace users run 1–2k concurrent sessions sometimes; batching behavior matters a lot.
[01:23] Jonah: Understood. Redwood's runtime supports continuous batching and KV cache — for marketplace flows with repeated prompts we should see token savings. For the benchmark we'll test both cold and warm cache scenarios.
[01:35] Markus: Also, what about private deployments? A lot of our enterprise customers ask for VPC or on-prem options. It's a blocker for some deals.
[01:42] Priya: Redwood Private supports VPC and an on-prem package; however, the timeline to onboard a private instance is longer than hosted. For time-sensitive pilots, we recommend hosted with a strict data-retention agreement, then move to Private for production.
[01:57] Ethan: OK. Can you outline typical time to production for private vs dedicated? Our PM wants numbers.
[02:04] Maya: Typical onboarding: hosted API — minutes to prod; Dedicated — 2–6 weeks for capacity provisioning and testing; Private (VPC/on-prem) — 6–12 weeks depending on network approvals and KMS integrations. We'll put that in the follow-up doc.

[02:20] Jonah: For benchmarks, we'll measure: p50/p95 latency, tokens per response, gateway overhead, and cost per 1k tokens. We'll give you the runbook so your SEs can replay it in your environment.
[02:33] Lina: Do you need sample prompts or can we use our anonymized production prompts?
[02:37] Jonah: Prefer production-like prompts; anonymized is fine. Also include typical sequence length distributions so we can choose the kernel and batching parameters appropriately.
[02:47] Ethan: On the contract side, two asks: escrow for data (we have customers asking for stronger data guarantees), and audit logs for every request for compliance.
[02:55] Priya: Redwood logs requests and supports audit exports; for escrow-style requirements we recommend dedicated or private deployments — hosted can be negotiated case-by-case. We'll include an audit log export example in the packet.
[03:10] Markus: We also want to avoid finger-pointing on incidents. Is there a standard joint-incident playbook for partner-resold customers?
[03:18] Maya: Yes — Redwood and partner ops can do a joint-runbook. We'll propose an SLA ladder and an on-call rotation as part of the pilot SOW.
[03:26] Ethan: Great. Let's talk about deal selection — which customers should we nominate? We want ones that 1) are likely to sign quickly, 2) show typical load profiles, and 3) are referenceable.
[03:36] Lina: We have two in mind: RetailCo (high-concurrency chat for customer service) and FinServX (sensitive data, needs KMS). RetailCo might be the faster win.
[03:45] Jonah: For RetailCo we should demo caching benefits and an A/B showing cost delta when applying prefix caching and quantization. For FinServX we'd propose a private pilot with KMS and stricter logging.
[03:57] Ethan: For RetailCo timeline, they could be ready by mid-November if we start this week.
[04:02] Maya: Ok — we'll aim to have the benchmark and GTM packet to you early next week so RetailCo can be onboarded by 11/15 if all goes well.
[04:10] Lina: On the engineering side, what integration points do we need? API keys, webhooks, and a proxy for traffic shaping?
[04:18] Jonah: API keys and token scoping are standard. For traffic shaping we recommend using Redwood's routing policies to split traffic between hosted and a lower-cost model variant during rollouts. We can supply example Nginx proxy patterns if you need local shaping.
[04:33] Ethan: How do we handle model updates and compatibility? We sell across multiple verticals and can't have model regressions mid-deal.
[04:41] Priya: Redwood supports pinned model versions and rollout policies including automatic fallback. We also do eval-based regression alerts tied to a prompt set. We'll include our eval template.
[04:52] Markus: Competitors — we've seen interest in Anthropic for compliance messaging and Vertex for cloud tie-ins. How do we position Redwood?
[04:59] Maya: Focus on production economics and unified deployment — predictable latency, cost levers, and private deployment options. We'll prepare a short battlecard comparing Redwood to Anthropic and Vertex focused on latency SLOs, cost per token, and private deployment timelines.
[05:13] Jonah: Technical note — quantization profiles can reduce GPU requirements for Reseller SKUs; we'll show both fp16 and 4-bit benchmarks in the run.
[05:22] Lina: That helps. For the benchmark, can you include a scenario that simulates 1k concurrent sessions?
[05:27] Jonah: We'll create a simulated client load that hits those concurrency levels and provides p50/p95 plus error rates. Expect the initial run to be in a sandbox environment.
[05:36] Ethan: On enablement — we need a one-pager for our sales team and a 30-minute enablement session. Can Redwood run that?
[05:42] Maya: Yes — we'll do a 30-minute enablement + Q&A in week after the benchmark. We'll record and share slides.
[05:50] Markus: Anything we should be aware of in terms of legal? Resale contract templates?
[05:54] Priya: We have a partner Reseller Addendum template — we'll attach it. For larger accounts we'll discuss indemnity clauses case-by-case.
[06:03] Ethan: Great. To recap — benchmark runbook and GTM one-pager from Redwood early next week, CloudMarket to pick pilot customers and share contact info, then we target a partner kickoff on 2026-11-09.
[06:14] Maya: Correct. I'll own the GTM packet and pricing. Jonah owns the benchmark. Priya will draft compensation plan.
[06:22] Lina: Quick clarification — pricing matrix should show hosted vs dedicated vs private and an example TCO for a 12-month committed volume.
[06:30] Maya: We'll include that.
[06:33] Markus: One last ops question — will Redwood handle refunds or credits if there's an SLA miss for a partner-resold customer?
[06:40] Priya: We'll propose SLA credit language in the SOW, typically credits tied to the partner contract. We'll map responsibilities in the joint incident playbook.
[06:49] Ethan: OK, good. No other items. Thanks everyone.
[06:52] Maya: Thanks — we'll follow up with the packet and schedule.

End recap:
- Redwood: send GTM one-pager, pricing matrix, SOC2/KMS docs, audit log example, reseller addendum, and benchmark runbook.
- Redwood SE: provision 48-hour benchmark window and share run instructions.
- CloudMarket: finalize two pilot customers and provide contact info for intros.
- Joint: schedule partner kickoff on 2026-11-09 and sales enablement session following benchmark.

Links shared (in chat): https://redwood.example.com/partner/guides, https://redwood.example.com/security/soc2-packet, placeholder bench sheet link
